youtube.title: Norway’s Interest Burden Failed This Credit-Risk Test
youtube.description:
Does household interest burden improve the next forecast of payment strain? The answer is a disciplined warning for credit committees.

Our forward holdout produced 0.573 pp MAE for the burden model versus 0.475 pp for persistence. The richer model did not win, so the ratio remains a stress trigger—not a stand-alone forecasting engine. Latest-vintage test; survey strain is not exposure-weighted PD. Source: SSB tables 08727 and 12128, release 22 Nov 2026.

youtube.title: EUR/NOK: Does the Norges Bank Rate Signal Actually Work?
youtube.description:
Can the policy-rate differential forecast the krone better than no change? This test separates an economic story from a usable signal.

The candidate MAPE was 1.406% versus 1.471% for the benchmark, but the uncertainty interval crosses zero. The edge is not decisive and does not represent a tradable strategy. Sources: Norges Bank policy and exchange-rate data, release 22 Nov 2026.

instagram.text:
A persuasive central-bank story is not automatically a trading signal.

For EUR/NOK, the policy-rate model reached 1.406% MAPE versus 1.471% for no change. The numerical edge is small, and its uncertainty interval includes zero.

For treasury teams: use the differential conditionally alongside risk appetite, oil and liquidity—not as an autonomous directional rule. This is a latest-vintage holdout, not a cost-adjusted strategy.

youtube.title: NBIM: When Capital Ownership and Voting Influence Diverge
youtube.description:
How often does portfolio ownership differ from recorded voting influence? This reconciliation maps where capital and voice separate.

Across 7,077 matched holdings, the value-weighted absolute gap is 0.093 pp. 410 holdings exceed 0.10 pp and represent 12.89% of matched portfolio value. This does not prove governance failure or infer intent. Sources: NBIM holdings and voting records, release 22 Nov 2026.

#NBIM #Stewardship #CorporateGovernance #VotingRights #AssetOwnership

instagram.text:
Capital ownership and voting influence are not the same exposure.

Across 7,077 matched NBIM holdings, the weighted absolute mismatch is 0.093 pp. 410 holdings exceed a 0.10 pp gap, representing 12.89% of matched value.

The right response is reconciliation—not accusation: share class, record date, lending and market rules can explain differences. Automated matching does not establish intent.

youtube.title: Europe’s AI Gap Is a Conversion Problem, Not Just Access
youtube.description:
Why do digitally ready economies still differ in business AI adoption? This cross-country test measures the missing conversion step.

Across ten countries, digital intensity and 2025 AI adoption correlate at 0.937. Leave-one-country-out MAE is 2.462 pp versus 8.762 pp for the baseline. Strong association is not causal proof or a temporal backtest. Source: Eurostat, release 22 Nov 2026.

instagram.text:
Europe’s AI adoption gap is increasingly a conversion gap.

For ten countries, digital intensity correlates 0.937 with enterprise AI use in 2025. Leave-one-country-out error is 2.462 pp versus 8.762 pp for the country baseline.

The policy implication is organizational: clean data, process redesign, skills and accountability determine whether infrastructure becomes production. Ten countries are not causal proof.

youtube.title: Norway’s Museums: Attendance Up, Funding Risk Still High
youtube.description:
